3.The appellants preferred reference application under section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (For short "the Act") being aggrieved by award dated 26.02.2010 passed by the Deputy Collector,
Land Acquisition & Rehabilitation, SIPU Project, Palanpur in LAQ Case No. 9 of 2008 under section 11(1) of the Act whereby Special Land Acquisition Officer awarded amount of compensation for the acquired agriculture land bearing Survey No. 1068 situated at Mouje Visnagar, Taluka Visnagar,
District Mahesana for the purpose of construction of Dharoi canal at the rate of Rs. 53/- per sq. mtr.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1903/2023 ORDER DATED: 20/07/2023 undefined

4.The appellants-claimants prayed for enhancement of the award amount from Rs.53/- to Rs.500/-
per sq. mtr. on the ground that notification under section 4 of the Act was published on 13.10.2008 and notification under section 6 of the Act was published on 11.08.2009 and the award of the Special Land Acquisition Officer declared on 26.02.2010 awarding Rs. 53/- per sq. mtr. was inadequate as the Special Land Acquisition Officer did not take into account three crops taken by the appellant during the year which included commercial crops like wheat, cotton, cumin seed etc.

According to the appellants- claimants, they were entitled to get compensation at the rate of Rs.
500/- per sq. mtr. and therefore, the amount awarded by the Special Land Acquisition Officer was inadequate, unjust and not reasonable.

5.It was also contended by the appellants- NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1903/2023 ORDER DATED: 20/07/2023 undefined claimants that the land of the claimants is situated in a well developed area, the same can also be used for non agriculture purposes and the adjoining lands are also used for commercial and industrial purpose.

It was also pointed out that educational institutions, transport facility, water and electric facility etc.
are also available near the acquired land.

6.The Reference Court considered the evidence led by the appellants-claimants and referred to and relied upon the Judgment and Award passed in LAR No.352 of 2009 wherein notification under section 4 of the Act was published on July, 2002 and compensation was awarded at Rs.500/- per sq.
mtr.
It was also declared before the Reference Court that no appeal is pending against the order passed in LAR No.352 of 2009 which pertains to the land acquired from the same village Visnagar.

NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1903/2023 ORDER DATED: 20/07/2023 undefined 7.Reference Court therefore, considering the date of notification under section 4 in the present case being 13.10.2008 i.e. almost after six years and three months, difference being 75 months between two notifications, calculated the amount payable to the appellants-claimants by giving price rise at 10% per year as under:
"price rise per year for 77 months.
As per simple interest formula S.I. PRT/100.

2 I.E. 500*10*77/12/100=312.5."
8.The

sentences.text: Reference Court therefore, held that total compensation payable as on the date of notification under section 4 in the present case would come to Rs.500/- + Rs.312.5 = Rs.812.5.

However,
Reference Court granted only Rs.500/- to the appellants-claimants on the ground that the claimants have demanded NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1903/2023 ORDER DATED: 20/07/2023 undefined only Rs.500/- and therefore, the claimants cannot be awarded compensation of more than Rs.500/-
per sq. mtr. and thus awarded only additional compensation of Rs.447/- per sq. mtr. with consequential solatium as provided under section 23(2) of the Act and interest as per the provisions of section 28 of the Act on the additional amount of compensation.

9.Learned advocate Mr. Ankur Kiri for the appellants submitted that the Reference Court could not have restricted the amount of compensation to amount of claim of Rs.500/- per sq. mtr. made by the appellants-claimants though the appellants are entitled to compensation of Rs.812.50.
It was therefore, submitted that the Court below has committed an error in restricting the compensation to Rs.500/- per sq. mtr.

9.1) In support of his submission, NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1903/2023 ORDER DATED:
20/07/2023 undefined reliance was placed on decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in case of Narendra & Ors. v. State of Uttar Pradesh & Ors.

entities.text: Narendra & Ors. v. State of Uttar Pradesh & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (Judgment dated 11.09.2017 passed in Civil Appeal Nos.10429-10430 of 2017), more particulalry, on para.5 of the said judgment wherein the Apex Court referred to and relied upon the decision in case of Ashok Kumar and Another v. State of Haryana reported in (2016) 4 SCC 544, wherein it is held that it is the duty of the Court to award just and fair compensation taking into consideration the true market value and other relevant factors, irrespective of the claim made by the landowner

entities.text: Ashok Kumar and Another v. State of Haryana reported in (2016) 4 SCC 544
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: and there is no cap on the maximum rate of compensation that can be awarded by the Court and the Courts are not restricted to award only the amount that has been claimed by the landowner/applicant in the application before it.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1903/2023 ORDER DATED: 20/07/2023 undefined 9.2)

It was therefore, submitted that the Reference Court ought to have awarded Rs.812.50 to the appellants-claimants and could not have restricted the compensation to Rs. 500/- per sq. mtr. as claimed by the appellants in their claim petition.

10. On the other hand learned AGP Ms.Hetal Patel submitted that the facts of the case before the Apex Court are totally different as two different awards were made for the same land by awarding different rates and therefore, in such circumstances, the Apex Court held that the claimants were entitled to compensation at the maximum rate awarded for the acquired land.

11. Having heard the learned advocates for the respective parties and having considered the documents on record, the only issue which arises for consideration is whether Reference NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1903/2023 ORDER DATED: 20/07/2023 undefined Court could have restricted the amount of compensation to Rs.500/- claimed by the appellants-claimants or not?

The issue is no more res integra in view of decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in case of Ashok Kumar and Another (supra) wherein it is held as under:
"6.
Prior to amendment Act 68 of 1984, the amount of compensation that could be awarded by the Court was limited to the amount claimed by the applicant.

Section 25 read as under- "Section 25. Rules as to amount of compensation-(1) When the applicant has made a claim to compensation, pursuant to any notice given Under Section 9, the amount awarded to him by the court shall not exceed the amount so claimed or be less than the amount awarded by the Collector Under Section 11.
(2) When the applicant has refused to make such claim or has omitted without sufficient reason (to be allowed by the Judge) to make such claim, the amount awarded by the court shall in no case exceed the amount awarded by the Collector.

NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1903/2023 ORDER DATED: 20/07/2023 undefined (3) When the applicant has omitted for a sufficient reason (to be allowed by the Judge) to make such claim, the amount awarded to him by the court shall not be less than, and may exceed, the amount awarded by the Collector."

The amended Section 25 reads as under:
"Section 25. Amount of compensation awarded by Court not to be lower than the amount awarded by the Collector- The amount of compensation awarded by the Court shall not be less than the amount awarded by the Collector under Section 11."
The amendment has come into effect on 24.09.1984.
7. The pre-amended provision put a cap on the maximum; the compensation by court should not be beyond the amount claimed.

The amendment in 1984, on the contrary, put a cap on the minimum;
compensation cannot be less that what was awarded by the Land Acquisition Collector.

The cap on maximum having been expressly omitted, and the cap that is put is only on minimum, it is clear that the amount of compensation that a court can award is no longer restricted to the amount claimed by the applicant.

It is the duty of the Court to award just and fair compensation taking into consideration the true market value and other relevant factors, irrespective of the claim made by NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1903/2023 ORDER DATED: 20/07/2023 undefined the owner.
8. xxx xxx
xxx 9.
In Bhag Singh and Ors. v. Union Territory of Chandigarh [(1985) 3 SCC 737], this Court held that there may be situations where the amount higher than claimed may be awarded to the claimant.

4 "3. ...

It must be remembered that this was not a dispute between two private citizens where it would be quite just and legitimate to confine the claimant to the claim made by him and not to award him any higher amount than that claimed though even in such a case there may be situations where an amount higher than that claimed can be awarded to the claimant as for instance where an amount is claimed as due at the foot of an account.

Here was a claim made by the Appellants against the State Government for compensation for acquisition of their land and under the law, the State was bound to pay to the Appellants compensation on the basis of the market value of the land acquired and if according to the judgments of the learned single Judge and the Division Bench, the market value of the land acquired was higher than that awarded by the Land Acquisition Collector or the Additional District Judge,
there is no reason why the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1903/2023 ORDER DATED:
20/07/2023 undefined Appellants should have been denied the benefit of payment of the market value so determined.
To deny this benefit to the Appellants would tantamount to permitting the State Government to acquire the land of the Appellants on payment of less than the true market value.

There may be cases where, as for instance, under' agrarian reform legislation, the holder of land may, legitimately, as a matter of social justice with a view to eliminating concentration of land in the hands of a few and bringing about its equitable distribution, be deprived of land which is not being personally cultivated by him or which is in excess of the ceiling area with payment of little compensation or no compensation at all, but where land is acquired under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, it would not be fair and just to deprive the holder of his land without payment of the true market value when the law, in so many terms, declares that he shall be paid such market value...."
13. The aforesaid decision was followed by the Apex Court in case of Narendra & Ors. (supra).

14. In view of above settled legal position, NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1903/2023 ORDER DATED:
20/07/2023 undefined the impugned Judgment and Award is modified and the compensation awarded by the Reference Court is enhanced to Rs.812.50 instead of Rs.500/- and the appellants are entitled to additional compensation of Rs.312.50 i.e. total additional compensation of Rs.759.50 in addition to Rs.53/- granted by the Special Land Acquisition Officer.
15. The appellants are also entitled to the consequential benefits under section 23(2) of the Act and interest as provided in terms of section 28 of the Act.

Additional enhanced compensation amount of Rs. 312.50 shall be paid to the appellants along with solatium at the rate of 30% as per section 23(2)
of the Act and interest at the rate of 12% on additional amount of compensation of Rs.312.50 under section 23(1A) of the Act along with interest at the rate of 9% per annum from the date of taking possession or NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1903/2023 ORDER DATED: 20/07/2023 undefined from the date of issuance of notification under section 4 of the Act, whichever is earlier, for first year and at the rate of 15% per annum till the realisation of the amount payable on aggregated enhanced amount of Rs. 312.50 as provided under section 28 of the Act within a period of 90 days from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
